From: Camila Reyes <camila.reyes@redwood.ai>

Subject: Post-call recap + structured-output evaluation plan for Acme Health

Hi Jenna / Martin — thanks again for the time today. Quick recap and proposed next steps from our side so we keep momentum: 

Summary of the call:
- Primary use case: structured triage for incoming patient messages (classify intent, extract entities for EHR intake) with strict downstream JSON schema enforcement.
- Key constraints: PII redaction required before any logs leave their VPC; latency target ~250ms p50 for single-turn inference; schema validation failure tolerance: must be <1% in production.
- Stakes: pilot aims to replace rule-based extractor for 3 clinics, potential expansion to enterprise contract if rollouts meet quality SLOs.

What Redwood will deliver (short list):
1) A focused eval harness that runs structured-output tests against your prompt set and target JSON schema.
2) Recommended model candidates and quantization profiles to balance cost/latency.
3) Baseline benchmark CSV + per-model token-cost estimate.
4) A small tool-calling test to validate function interfaces and retry semantics.

Immediate next steps (proposed):
- Action A (you): Share final prompt set (you already uploaded acme_prompt_set_v1.json; please confirm poset).
- Action B (Redwood): Run a 10k-sample structured-output pass against the schema you sent; include both strict schema check (fail on type/required) and graceful-fill path for missing optional fields.
- Action C (SRE/legal): We’ll prepare a short SOC2 evidence checklist for the pilot.

Schedule: we can start the run Monday (8/28) if you confirm the prompt set and grant read access to the sample corpus in the Drive link above.

Attachments: acme_inference_requirements.docx (requirements summary), acme_prompt_set_v1.json (prompt set stub), baseline_benchmarks.csv (previous internal baseline).

Questions for you:
- Can we get a short sample of 1k real messages (PII redacted) by EOD Monday?
- Are you comfortable with Redwood provisioning short-term test keys scoped to the Acme pilot VPC, or do you prefer we run entirely on your infra?

Thanks — I’ll coordinate with Sergio on the model/benchmark side.

Best,
Camila Reyes

Thanks Camila — proposing the following concrete evaluation plan from SRE/SE side: 

1) Model candidates (initial pass):
   - redwood/clarity-7B (FP16) — low-latency baseline, expected p50 ~160ms on C-class GPU with batching 1–4.
   - redwood/forte-13B-quant (8-bit) — better nominal extraction recall on complex prompts, p50 ~240ms.
   - redwood/echo-70B-quant (16-bit-quant) — higher-quality fallback for edge cases (higher cost).

2) Run matrix:
   - 10k structured-inputs (mix of 1k real redacted + 9k synthesized variants)
   - For each model: run strict schema validator + graceful-fill pass. Output: per-sample pass/fail + error type tag (type_mismatch, missing_required, extra_field, enum_invalid, parse_error).
   - A/B: compute per-field F1 vs Acme baseline extractor (baseline_benchmarks.csv attached). Also compute macro-average JSON schema pass rate.

3) Tool/function calling test:
   - Validate the function contract using a small harness that simulates downstream function endpoints (EHR insert). Tests: success path, transient 5xx with retry (exponential backoff with jitter), idempotency key check. We’ll log retry counts and failure modes.

4) Regression guardrails:
   - If any model shows >5% drop in macro-F1 for critical entity set (patient_name, DOB, medication) vs baseline, we flag as regression.
   - Produce a CSV of failing samples for manual triage (redaction preserved).

5) Deliverables (timeline):
   - Wed 8/30 EOD: initial run results (per-model CSV + aggregated report + failure buckets)
   - Thu 8/31: short sync to review results and pick pilot model; if pick is agreed, start pilot provisioning.

Operational notes:
- We will provision time-limited API keys and set up KMS wrapping for any artifacts. Our run will not store raw PII outside encrypted artifacts.
- Latency: we’ll include p50/p95 and a batch-size sensitivity chart.

Questions for Jenna/Martin (quick):
- Do you want the strict-schema run to fail the sample or to store the partial structured output (graceful-fill)? We can produce both, but need to know which you prefer as the primary metric.

Sergio
